subject: Clarify billing granularity for streaming calls + annual rebate structure
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@lumahealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@lumahealth.com
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Billing details for telemedicine transcription pilot (SOW attached)

Hi Stephanie / Jordan,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attaching the SOW and a small sample of usage to help the procurement team size things: Luma_Hall_SOW_v2.pdf (see attachment) and a CSV with 10 sample sessions.

Before we move to signature we need a clear, contractible definition for two things that our legal/procurement teams flagged:

1) How will you bill streaming transcription on a hybrid contract? We're combining a seat-based committed SKU for routing/priority with a pay-as-you-go transcription stream. Procurement asked whether streaming will be measured per-token, per-minute, or some blended "per-minute-equivalent" derived from tokens. They want deterministic rounding rules so monthly invoices don't vary unpredictably.

2) How does the annual rebate/commit interplay with the streaming consumption? Specifically: if we commit $X/year with a tiered rebate that kicks in at >80% consumption, how do you apportion streaming usage that is only billed per minute in some months and token-heavy in others? Will credits/rebates be pro-rated monthly or applied at true-up?

A couple of other concerns: multi-language sessions (mix of English and Mandarin) that tokenize differently — procurement wants to avoid surprises from tokenization quirks.

Can you provide an example invoice for a month with 1) 120 reserved-seat days used, 2) 45,000 tokens from model A streaming, and 3) 300 minutes of live transcription (mixed languages)? Also please call out any minimums or rounding we should expect.

Thanks — we need the language to be explicit in the SOW before legal signs.

Best,
Olivia
Head of Engineering Operations
Luma Health

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 12:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Billing details for telemedicine transcription pilot (SOW attached)

Hi Olivia — thanks for the SOW and the sample. Quick overview below, plus a worked example attached (billing_walkthrough.xlsx). Happy to iterate contract language once you confirm the approach.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Primary billing primitives: reserved-seat commitment (monthly/seat-day accounting) + streaming consumption.
- For streaming transcription we propose a "per-minute-equivalent" billing footprint that maps to tokens using a model-specific conversion profile (we provide the conversion table in the walkthrough). For invoices we will show both raw tokens and the mapped minutes so you can reconcile to clinical minutes.
- Rounding rules:
  * For short events (<15s) we will aggregate into a 30s quantum for billing (to avoid micro-charges).
  * After aggregation, streaming totals are converted to the billing primitive and then rounded up to the nearest 10 token quantum for token-derived charges (this is only applied to the token side after the minute-equivalent mapping).
- Multi-language handling: we will apply a language normalization multiplier for tokens derived from non-ASCII heavy content; we suggest a conservative 1.05 multiplier for CJK-heavy transcripts to account for tokenization density. We can provide per-model multipliers validated on your sample set.

Worked example (summary — full calc in attachment):
- Reserved seat costs: charged per seat-day, no rounding.
- Streaming: raw tokens (45,000) -> model A profile says 1 clinical minute ≈ 210 tokens -> mapped minutes = 45,000 / 210 ≈ 214.29 minutes. Apply aggregation: remaining micro-events rounded into 30s buckets -> mapped minutes round up to 214.5 -> final billed tokens equivalent (after quantization) = ceil(214.5 * 210 / 10) * 10 = 45,030 tokens billed.

Rebates/annual commit:
- We recommend applying the tiered rebate as a pro-rated credit applied monthly to invoices (so your monthly invoices reflect progress toward the annual threshold). True-up invoice at contract year-end will reconcile any over/under-crediting. This avoids a sudden one-time negative invoice while giving you visibility.

I'll loop in Jordan for the exact clause language and Vivek for the technical multiplier validation.

Next steps: Jordan, can you draft a short paragraph for the SOW that captures the rounding/aggregation rules and a line about monthly pro-rated rebate credits? Olivia — once you confirm the approach I'll produce a one-paragraph addendum you can attach to the SOW.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@lumahealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 10:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Billing details for telemedicine transcription pilot (SOW attached)

Thanks — drafting suggested contract language below for quick review. This is intentionally concise so it can be pasted into the SOW and into procurement redlines: please flag any items you want tightened.

Proposed SOW clause (billing units & rebate treatment):
"Streaming transcription consumption will be reported as raw token usage per invoice. For customer convenience and reconciliation to clinical time, Redwood will also provide a model-specific tokens-to-minutes conversion table. For billing purposes, streaming sessions shorter than 15 seconds will be aggregated into 30-second billing quanta. After aggregation, consumption will be normalized to a per-token equivalent using the agreed model profile and rounded up to the nearest 10-token billing quantum. For sessions where non-Latin character sets materially affect token counts, a pre-agreed normalization multiplier (e.g., 1.05 for specified CJK-heavy workloads) will be applied prior to rounding.

Tiered rebate: Annual committed-spend rebates will be calculated on total billed consumption (reserved + streaming) and applied as a monthly pro-rated credit to invoices. Redwood will deliver a year-end true-up invoice to reconcile final rebate amounts against credits applied during the contract year."

Operational notes:
- We will include raw-token and mapped-minute lines on every invoice so you can reconcile with clinical systems.
- For the pilot concession: Redwood agrees to apply any rebate that would have been due in Q1/Q2 as credits in the month following each quarter (to help cashflow).

Vivek — can you confirm the 1.05 multiplier threshold and whether we should lock it per model or per dataset?

Olivia — if this looks okay I can turn it into a single-paragraph addendum for the SOW and route for signature.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Director, Sales Operations
